cues.en: This is the fourth video in my Strong Town series.
cues.zh: 这是我的“强镇”（Strong Town）系列视频的第四期。

cues.en: You probably want to watch at least the last two videos to properly understand this one.
cues.zh: 你可能至少要先看前两期视频，才能更好地理解这一期。

cues.en: When some people see the growth Ponzi scheme graph for the first time, they may ask, we've been building car dependent sprawls since the nineteen fifties. Why are the suburbs still here? Shouldn't they all have gone bankrupt by now? And it's a completely reasonable question.
cues.zh: 有些人第一次看到增长庞氏骗局的图表时可能会问：我们从二十世纪五十年代起就一直在建设依赖汽车的蔓延式郊区，为什么这些郊区现在还在？它们不是早该破产了吗？这是一个完全合理的问题。

cues.en: Of course, there have been cities in The US that have gone bankrupt.
cues.zh: 当然，美国确实有城市破产过。

cues.en: Detroit, Michigan is the example most people think of, but there have been several others such as Vallejo, California
cues.zh: 密歇根州的底特律是大多数人首先想到的例子，但还有其他几个，比如加利福尼亚州的瓦列霍

cues.en: or Jefferson County, Alabama
cues.zh: 或者阿拉巴马州的杰斐逊县

cues.en: and Washington Park, Illinois
cues.zh: 还有伊利诺伊州的华盛顿公园

cues.en: and Moffett, Oklahoma have declared bankruptcy twice.
cues.zh: 以及俄克拉荷马州的莫弗特，它已经宣布破产两次了。

cues.en: But before you jump on any of these particular examples you should know that only 27 states even allow municipalities
cues.zh: 但在你拿这些例子说事之前，你要知道，全美只有27个州允许地方政府

cues.en: to declare bankruptcy and of those 15 have special conditions or limitations.
cues.zh: 申请破产，而且其中15个州还有特殊条件或限制。

cues.en: So bankruptcies are not telling the whole story.
cues.zh: 所以破产并不能说明全部情况。

cues.en: Nevertheless,
cues.zh: 尽管如此，

cues.en: most car dependent places are still here. So why is this?
cues.zh: 大多数依赖汽车的地方如今依然存在。这是为什么呢？

cues.en: Before we get into the answer to that question, let's talk about how American cities used to be built.
cues.zh: 在回答这个问题之前，我们先聊聊美国的城市过去是怎么建设的。

cues.en: Consider an early city. It would start as a collection of shacks along a road or railroad like this one.
cues.zh: 设想一座早期城市。它最初可能像这样，只是沿着一条公路或铁路搭建的一片棚屋。

cues.en: A small number of people here would make some bets on the future and build their houses and shops nearby.
cues.zh: 这里有一小部分人会对未来下注，在附近盖起自己的房子和店铺。

cues.en: Many of these attempts may have failed, but others were successful too like this one.
cues.zh: 其中很多尝试可能失败了，但也有成功的，就像这一处。

cues.en: So the shacks became more permanent structures, and they could now afford to build some basic road and water infrastructure.
cues.zh: 于是棚屋逐渐变成了更坚固的建筑，这时他们也有能力修建一些基本的道路和供水基础设施了。

cues.en: As more time passed, the buildings became made of stone and granite.
cues.zh: 随着时间推移，建筑变成了石头和花岗岩筑成的。

cues.en: There was a permanence to it. A proper sewage system was built and the roads were upgraded.
cues.zh: 这里有了一种持久感。修建了像样的排污系统，道路也得到了升级。

cues.en: This would attract more people and the city would gradually grow outwards.
cues.zh: 这会吸引更多人前来，城市逐渐向外扩张。

cues.en: Most importantly,
cues.zh: 最重要的是，

cues.en: as this place grew, it would build the wealth needed to sustain it.
cues.zh: 随着这个地方的发展，它积累了维持自身运转所需的财富。

cues.en: A place like this is never finished.
cues.zh: 这样的地方永远不会真正完工。

cues.en: Some parts will succeed and build up. Others will fail and change their land use.
cues.zh: 有些部分会成功并不断向上发展，有些则会失败并改变土地用途。

cues.en: But in post World War two America,
cues.zh: 但在二战后的美国，

cues.en: this approach changed completely.
cues.zh: 这种模式彻底改变了。

cues.en: Instead of incrementally building upon the places they already had,
cues.zh: 美国城市不再在他们已有的地方上逐步建设，

cues.en: American cities started building brand new places to a completed state in new neighborhoods on the edge of town and left their existing places to rot away.
cues.zh: 而是在城镇边缘的新街区里，把全新的地方一次性建到“完工”状态，任由原有的老城区慢慢烂掉。

cues.en: Remember this photo from earlier?
cues.zh: 还记得前面这张照片吗？

cues.en: It's Front Street in Brainerd, Minnesota 1871.
cues.zh: 这是明尼苏达州布雷纳德的前街，1871年。

cues.en: In nineteen o five, it looked like this.
cues.zh: 1905年时，它是这个样子。

cues.en: And this is what it looks like today
cues.zh: 而今天它是这个样子

cues.en: Because as prosuburbanization
cues.zh: 因为随着鼓励郊区化的

cues.en: policies came into place, it became cheaper and easier to build new buildings on the edge of town rather than to improve the places that already existed.
cues.zh: 政策出台，在城镇边缘建新楼变得比改造现有城区更便宜、更容易。

cues.en: People used to be so proud of this place that they had built that they put it on postcards.
cues.zh: 人们曾经为自己建起的这个地方感到无比自豪，甚至把它印在了明信片上。

cues.en: Nobody is making a postcard of this place.
cues.zh: 没人会把这地方印在明信片上。

cues.en: Incidentally,
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，

cues.en: this is something that really bothers me when Americans claim they can't be like European cities because their cities were built for the car.
cues.zh: 美国人声称他们无法像欧洲城市那样发展，因为他们的城市是为汽车而建的，这一点真的让我很困扰。

cues.en: This street wasn't built for the car. It was bulldozed for the car. It didn't have to be this way.
cues.zh: 这条街道不是为汽车而建造的，而是为汽车被推平重建的。事情本不必变成这样。

cues.en: But it's true that American suburbia was built to be car dependent.
cues.zh: 但确实，美国郊区当初就是按照依赖汽车出行的模式来规划的。

cues.en: You need an automobile to do just about anything.
cues.zh: 做什么事几乎都得有辆车。

cues.en: But even more important is how differently these places were built and funded compared to anything that had ever been built before.
cues.zh: 但更重要的是，这些地方的建造和融资方式，都和此前建成的任何地方截然不同。

cues.en: This infrastructure was not built using existing wealth.
cues.zh: 这套基础设施并不是靠既有财富建成的。

cues.en: Instead,
cues.zh: 相反，

cues.en: in order to accelerate growth, federal and state funds were used to build these places paid for by government bonds.
cues.zh: 为了加快增长，这些场所是用联邦和州资金建造的，费用由政府债券支付。

cues.en: Chicagoans
cues.zh: 芝加哥人

cues.en: raised their share of the $92,000,000
cues.zh: 筹集了他们在那 9200 万美元中所占的份额

cues.en: cost by a bond issue.
cues.zh: 由发行债券来支付。

cues.en: Interest and retirement to be paid for by future revenue. Borrowing money to finance expansion is traditional with Americans.
cues.zh: 利息和退休金要靠未来收入来支付。借钱为扩张融资是美国人一贯的做法。

cues.en: The time and money saved
cues.zh: 节省下来的时间和金钱

cues.en: more than repays your investment.
cues.zh: 完全值得你的投入。

cues.en: If you wait to pay as you go,
cues.zh: 如果你等到按用量付费，

cues.en: you may not go at all.
cues.zh: 你可能根本就不会去。

cues.en: Now you could argue that debt in itself isn't necessarily
cues.zh: 现在你可能会说，技术债本身不一定……

cues.en: a problem as long as that debt can be repaid.
cues.zh: 只要那笔债还得清，就不算问题。

cues.en: But as we've discussed in previous episodes,
cues.zh: 但正如我们在前几期节目中讨论过的，

cues.en: sprawling car dependent places cannot sustain themselves.
cues.zh: 蔓延扩张、依赖汽车的城市形态是无法自我维系的。

cues.en: The amount of tax revenue collected is not sufficient to cover the replacement cost of the infrastructure.
cues.zh: 所征收的税款总额不足以支付基础设施的更新成本。

cues.en: The roads, electrical wires, water pipes and wastewater systems are spread out over a huge area while servicing very few people who actually pay for it.
cues.zh: 道路、电线、水管和污水系统分布在广袤的区域上，而服务的实际付费用户却非常少。

cues.en: This creates an illusion of wealth. These cities and suburbs look wealthy because of their new infrastructure,
cues.zh: 这营造出一种富裕的假象。这些城市和郊区看起来很富裕，因为它们有了新的基础设施，

cues.en: but in the long term, they're financially insolvent.
cues.zh: 但从长远来看，它们在财务上是难以为继的。

cues.en: But the effects of this are not seen until that infrastructure is due to be replaced, which only starts to happen after about twenty five years.
cues.zh: 但这种影响要到该基础设施需要更换时才会显现，而更换大约25年后才开始。

cues.en: When these infrastructure maintenance bills come due, the city needs to find a way to pay for them. And if the city is not growing, they can't just sweep the problem under the rug.
cues.zh: 当这些基础设施维护账单到期时，城市需要想办法支付。而如果城市不再增长，他们也不能把问题掩盖过去。

cues.en: The first reaction of many people is to just increase tax revenues.
cues.zh: 很多人的第一反应就是直接增加税收。

cues.en: But this shows a lack of understanding of the scale of the problem.
cues.zh: 但这说明了对问题规模缺乏理解。

cues.en: Strong Towns has several examples from actual real world cities and towns.
cues.zh: Strong Towns 中有多个来自真实世界城市和城镇的实际案例。

cues.en: Tampa, Florida for example needs to pay $3,200,000,000
cues.zh: 例如，佛罗里达州坦帕需要支付 3,200,000,000 美元

cues.en: to repair its water systems requiring an eight times increase in spending.
cues.zh: 为了修缮其供水系统，支出需要增加八倍。

cues.en: Fun fact: Tampa already pays more in debt payments on water infrastructure than it spends on maintaining water infrastructure.
cues.zh: 有趣的是：坦帕市在水务基础设施债务偿还上的支出，已经超过了它用于维护水务基础设施的支出。

cues.en: An extreme case is the small town of Backus, Minnesota, which was at the end of life of its wastewater system.
cues.zh: 一个极端案例是明尼苏达州的小镇巴克斯（Backus），它的污水处理系统已经到了使用寿命的尽头。

cues.en: But because this town was made up of sprawling low productivity car centric infrastructure,
cues.zh: 但因为这个镇是由低效蔓延、以汽车为中心的基础设施构成的，

cues.en: the wastewater system was sprawling and wasteful as well.
cues.zh: 它的污水处理系统也同样蔓延而浪费。

cues.en: This replacement cost was $27,000
cues.zh: 这次更换的费用是每户 27,000 美元

cues.en: per family
cues.zh: 相当于镇上家庭的

cues.en: which was the median household income in the town.
cues.zh: 中位数年收入。

cues.en: You can't just tax people their entire yearly income.
cues.zh: 你不可能直接向人们征收他们整整一年的收入。

cues.en: Of course, in any sane country, a small low density town wouldn't have a wastewater system.
cues.zh: 当然，在任何理智的国家，一个低密度的小镇根本不会有污水处理系统。

cues.en: Each home would have its own septic tank maintained by the household.
cues.zh: 每户人家都会有自己的化粪池，由住户自行维护。

cues.en: But this is the problem with the American mentality around car dependent sprawl.
cues.zh: 但这就是美国人对汽车依赖型蔓延的心态问题所在。

cues.en: Everybody expects urban services with near rural densities.
cues.zh: 人人都期待以近乎乡村的密度享受城市服务。

cues.en: Municipal water and sewer systems, buried electrical cables, traffic lights, garbage collection, fully paved multi lane arterial roads to every neighborhood. But they're not willing to actually pay for it.
cues.zh: 市政供水和排污系统、地下电缆、交通信号灯、垃圾清运、通往每个社区的全铺装多车道主干道。但他们并不愿意真正为此买单。

cues.en: The American dream never said nothing about maintaining your own septic tank.
cues.zh: 美国梦可从来没说过要自己维护化粪池。

cues.en: So in an American town placed in this situation takes money from federal and state governments and rebuilds the wastewater system.
cues.zh: 所以一个陷入这种境地的美国小镇，就会从联邦和州政府拿钱，重建污水处理系统。

cues.en: Here's another small town in Minnesota that had the same problem and their bailout package looked like this.
cues.zh: 明尼苏达州还有另一个遇到同样问题的小镇，他们的救助方案是这样的。

cues.en: This single wastewater project amounted to 37 times the amount raised annually from property taxes.
cues.zh: 仅这一个污水项目，就相当于该镇每年通过房产税筹集资金的 37 倍。

cues.en: You may think that talking about cities this way in terms of their finances is crude or excessively neoliberal.
cues.zh: 你可能会觉得，这样从财务角度谈论城市，显得粗俗，或者过于“新自由主义”。

cues.en: After all, cities are much more than their balance sheet and not everything in a city needs to turn a profit.
cues.zh: 毕竟，城市远不止是一张资产负债表，也不是城市里的一切都需要盈利。

cues.en: But ultimately,
cues.zh: 但归根结底，

cues.en: in order to provide a high quality of life in your town or city, you need to have the money to actually pay for services.
cues.zh: 要想让你的城镇提供高质量的生活，你就得有钱真正支付这些服务的费用。

cues.en: There are regular articles in The US about cities closing libraries,
cues.zh: 美国经常有报道称，一些城市关闭图书馆，

cues.en: turning off street lights overnight,
cues.zh: 夜间关闭路灯，

cues.en: or deferring road maintenance so much that their roads become worse than Belgium's.
cues.zh: 或者把道路维护一拖再拖，以至于路况变得比比利时的还糟。

cues.en: You can't make your city great if you're financially insolvent.
cues.zh: 如果城市在财务上资不抵债，你就不可能让它变得伟大。

cues.en: Incidentally,
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，

cues.en: Canadian cities are somewhat insulated from this problem because there are legal debt limits for many cities in Canada.
cues.zh: 加拿大的城市在一定程度上能免受这个问题的困扰，因为加拿大许多城市都有法定债务上限。

cues.en: For example, in Ontario,
cues.zh: 例如在安大略省，

cues.en: annual debt repayments cannot exceed 25 of a city's revenue.
cues.zh: 年度债务偿还额不得超过城市收入的 25%。

cues.en: Though keep in mind that there's no such limit on provincial debt and ultimately the province may be paying for a lot of that new infrastructure.
cues.zh: 不过要注意，省级债务没有这样的限制，最终很多新基础设施可能是由省政府来买单的。

cues.en: Now as we've discussed in previous videos, a growing city can just build more developments on the edge of town.
cues.zh: 正如我们在之前的视频中讨论过的，一个正在增长的城市可以不断在城镇边缘开发新的项目。

cues.en: This provides a quick influx of new tax revenue and this can be used to pay for the previous generation of infrastructure liabilities.
cues.zh: 这会带来新税收的快速涌入，而这些收入可以用来偿还上一代基础设施的债务。

cues.en: Again, this isn't built on the wealth of places that already exist. It's building new places in the suburbs even as existing inner ring suburbs may be falling into disrepair.
cues.zh: 同样，这并非建立在现有区域的财富之上。而是在既有的内环郊区逐渐破败的同时，继续在郊区开辟新区。

cues.en: To create this growth, the city needs to build out new infrastructure
cues.zh: 为了实现这种增长，城市需要铺设新的基础设施，

cues.en: and that is usually paid for with a mix of funds from federal and state governments as well as debt.
cues.zh: 资金通常来自联邦与州政府的拨款，以及发行债务。

cues.en: This chart shows the increase in US public sector debt since the 1950s.
cues.zh: 这张图表展示了自 1950 年代以来美国公共部门债务的增长情况。

cues.en: And you can see where the first and second generation of suburban infrastructure liabilities comes due.
cues.zh: 你能看到第一代和第二代郊区基础设施债务在何时到期。

cues.en: Now when you plot this public sector debt against US GDP, you might argue that the levels of debt seem proportional.
cues.zh: 现在，如果把这笔公共债务与美国 GDP 进行对比，你可能会觉得两者的比例还算合理。

cues.en: I'm not going to get into that. But this graph is hiding something.
cues.zh: 我暂且不深究这个，但这张图表隐瞒了一些真相。

cues.en: Because while local governments take on their own debt to build infrastructure,
cues.zh: 因为地方政府虽然举债修建了基础设施，

cues.en: eventually somebody needs to actually buy the houses and businesses,
cues.zh: 但最终总得有人去买下这些房屋和商铺，

cues.en: usually with debt and mortgages.
cues.zh: 而这通常也是靠借贷和房贷。

cues.en: In the first generation of car dependent suburbia,
cues.zh: 在依赖汽车的第一代郊区化时期，

cues.en: this private sector debt was minimal.
cues.zh: 这种私营部门的债务还微乎其微。

cues.en: But look at what happens as we get into the second and third generation of the suburban experiment.
cues.zh: 但看看当郊区实验进入第二代和第三代时，发生了什么。

cues.en: Here you can start to see how, instead of building on wealth that already exists in cities,
cues.zh: 从这里你就能看出，美国并没有在城市现有的财富基础上发展，

cues.en: America is financing its insolvent car dependent sprawl by heavily indebted its citizens to fund that growth.
cues.zh: 而是让普通民众背负沉重债务，以此来为这种注定资不抵债、依赖汽车的无序扩张买单。

cues.en: But don't worry, after the two thousand eight financial crisis everyone realized their mistake and it's all fine now.
cues.zh: 不过别担心，2008 年金融危机之后大家就都醒悟了，现在一切都好得很。

cues.en: Of course, there's way more to this than just suburbia.
cues.zh: 当然，背后的问题远不止郊区化这么简单。

cues.en: The entire American economy is built on a dangerous dependence on debt and growth. But that's getting far beyond the topic of this video or even this YouTube channel.
cues.zh: 整个美国经济都建立在对债务和增长的危险依赖之上。但这已经远远超出了本期视频甚至本 YouTube 频道的探讨范围。

cues.en: So let's get back to talking about cities.
cues.zh: 所以我们还是言归正传，聊聊城市。

cues.en: We need to reevaluate how cities are built and financed.
cues.zh: 我们需要重新审视城市的建设与融资模式。

cues.en: For centuries, cities were built by many people making small bets and as those places succeeded and generated wealth, they were upgraded and improved upon building successful cities.
cues.zh: 几个世纪以来，城市的建设都是由许多人一点点试探性投入构成的，随着这些区域走向成功并创造财富，它们不断升级改造，最终造就了繁荣的城市。

cues.en: But that means taking advantage of the infrastructure that already exists.
cues.zh: 但这意味着要充分利用现有的基础设施。

cues.en: Instead of constantly building out new public infrastructure,
cues.zh: 与其不断兴建新的公共基础设施，

cues.en: we need to densify the places that have already been created
cues.zh: 我们不如提高现有区域的开发密度，

cues.en: and build upon the wealth that's already there to make cities that can sustain themselves.
cues.zh: 依托现有的财富基础，打造能够自给自足的城市。

cues.en: Now low density suburbs and rural areas are fine too,
cues.zh: 当然，低密度的郊区和乡村也没什么不好，

cues.en: but these places can't expect the same level of services that you'd find in a major city.
cues.zh: 但这些地方不能指望享有和大城市完全同等水平的公共服务。

cues.en: In future videos in this series, we'll discuss which parts of cities operate at a loss and which parts keep them afloat and how the poorest Americans are subsidizing wealthy suburbanites.
cues.zh: 在本系列的后续视频中，我们将探讨城市的哪些区域在亏本运营、哪些在维持财政运转，以及美国最贫困的群体是如何补贴富裕的郊区居民的。

cues.en: But there are a few topics we need to discuss first,
cues.zh: 不过在此之前，我们还有几个话题要聊，

cues.en: like these awful places.
